On a vibrant night of football in West London, Fulham and Chelsea faced off in the Premier League International Cup on August 24, 2026. The atmosphere at the stadium, with over 27,000 fans in attendance, set the stage for an intense tactical battle between two rivals seeking supremacy in this prestigious competition. An Explosive Opening Half The match began in explosive fashion, with Chelsea taking the lead in the very first minute. Joao Pedro capitalized on a precise pass from Cole Palmer to beat Bernd Leno with a magnificent right-footed lob, momentarily silencing the home crowd. However, Fulham refused to be discouraged and began to apply pressure, finding their reward in the 23rd minute. Following a mistake from Robert Sanchez , Joshua King made no mistake, finishing with his right foot to restore parity and ignite the local supporters. The balance remained until shortly before the interval when the Blues accelerated once more. In the 41st minute, a well-crafted move resulted in a decisive assist from Maxence Lacroix for Morgan Rogers . The young forward had a simple tap-in to restore the visitors' lead before the break. The first half was also punctuated by yellow cards for Levi Colwill and Romeo Lavia , reflecting the aggression and competitive nature of the contest. Intensity and Drama Until the Final Whistle The second half started in the worst possible way for the Cottagers. In the 49th minute, a major blunder by Bernd Leno allowed Joao Pedro to set up Cole Palmer , who finished clinically with his left foot to extend the lead. While it seemed the game might be out of reach, Fulham reacted immediately. Just five minutes later, Gonzalo Garcia rose highest to head home, reducing the deficit to 3-2 and reigniting the contest. The final stages of the match were defined by a series of substitutions and rising tension. Timothy Castagne and Calvin Bassey were booked as they struggled to contain counter-attacks. In stoppage time, Fulham launched a desperate offensive, with Rodrigo Muniz and Gonzalo Garcia both seeing late efforts denied by the Chelsea defense and goalkeeper Robert Sanchez . Despite holding 61% of the possession, the hosts could not find a late equalizer, falling to a clinical Chelsea side.
